data.name: Saurabh
data.gender_notes: Saurabh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit words ‘sa’ (meaning good) and ‘ravi’ (meaning sun), Saurabh is a name that evokes the radiance and power of the sun god. In Hindu mythology, Saurabh is a title of the sun god Surya, and is also the name of a legendary sage and a warrior king. This name is believed to bring good fortune, courage, and strength to those who bear it.
data.etymology: Saurabh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Radiance of the Sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saurabh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_sanskrit.name: सौरभ

in_hindi.name: सौरभ
in_hindi.long_meaning: In Hindi, Saurabh is also understood to mean 'subtle, refined, and profound'. The word 'sukshma' in Hindi refers to something that is subtle and refined, while 'rightaa' means profound. Thus, Saurabh can also be interpreted as 'possessing a subtle, refined, and profound nature'.

vedic_reference.note: Saurabh is a popular name in Hindu mythology and is derived from the Sanskrit root 'सौ (sau)' meaning 'fragrance, pleasure, good, auspicious'. It is also mentioned in the Mahabharata, where it is the name of a king and a hero. Thus, Saurabh has a strong Vedic connection and is deeply rooted in Hindu culture.

historical_references.reference: Saurabh was a famous warrior and a commander-in-chief of the King Bhagiratha of Haihayas during the Mahabharata period. He played a significant role in the Kurukshetra war.
Saurabh was also known as Suryasena, a king of the Suryavanshi dynasty mentioned in the Ramayana. He was a friend and ally of Lord Rama during his exile and helped him in his war against Ravana.
